# STEPFOC

> Documentation for the STEPFOC stepper motor FOC driver by Source Robotics.

Every page of this site is also available as Markdown at its address followed by `index.md`, with its links absolute; `llms-full.txt` holds every page in one file. The version box on the landing page names the release the pages describe.


## STEPFOC Manual

- [STEPFOC Manual](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/index.md): Source Robotics d.o.o.
- [Quick start](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/quick-start/index.md): From the box to a calibrated motor that follows commands, on one page.
- [About this manual](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/about/index.md): The STEPFOC Manual covers the STEPFOC stepper driver from unpacking to a tuned motor on a CAN bus: what the driver is, how to mount it on a motor and wire it, the first setup over the serial terminal, calibration and tun
- [Overview](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/01-overview/index.md): What STEPFOC is and what it is made of, how it relates to the Spectral Micro BLDC driver it is built on, and what you need around it to get a motor turning.
- [The driver at a glance](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/01-overview/driver-at-a-glance/index.md): STEPFOC is a field-oriented controller for bipolar stepper motors.
- [STEPFOC and Spectral Micro](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/01-overview/stepfoc-and-spectral/index.md): STEPFOC and the Spectral Micro BLDC driver are sister drivers: similar hardware and similar firmware, each made for its kind of motor.
- [What you need](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/01-overview/what-you-need/index.md): This page lists what a STEPFOC setup is made of, what comes with the driver, and what you buy or make yourself.
- [2. Safety](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/02-safety/index.md): STEPFOC is a bare circuit board that drives a motor from a supply of up to 29 V.
- [Technical data](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/03-technical-data/index.md): The numbers: ratings and limits, the connectors with their pinout, the dimensions, and the motors that have been tested with the driver.
- [Ratings and limits](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/03-technical-data/ratings/index.md): The defaults of every setting are listed in the Defaults reference.
- [Connectors and pinout](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/03-technical-data/connectors/index.md)
- [Dimensions and CAD](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/03-technical-data/dimensions/index.md): The board is 39 × 39 mm with the four mounting holes on the NEMA 17 pattern (31 mm apart), so it bolts to the back of a NEMA 17 motor with the motor's own screws and a spacer.
- [Tested motors](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/03-technical-data/tested-motors/index.md): STEPFOC works with bipolar (4-wire) stepper motors whose phase resistance is 1 to 5 Ω and whose rated current is 3 A or less.
- [Mounting and wiring](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/04-mounting/index.md): How the driver goes onto the motor and what gets connected to it: the encoder magnet on the shaft, the board on the motor's back, the two coils to the motor terminals, the supply and the CAN bus, and the thermistor.
- [The encoder magnet](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/04-mounting/magnet/index.md): The encoder reads a diametrically magnetised magnet on the rear end of the motor shaft.
- [Mounting on the motor](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/04-mounting/mounting/index.md): The board has the NEMA 17 hole pattern (31 mm), so it mounts on the back of the motor with the motor's own four rear screws, with a spacer between the motor and the board that sets the magnet height.
- [Wiring the stepper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/04-mounting/wiring/index.md): A bipolar stepper has two coils and four wires.
- [Power and the CAN daisy chain](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/04-mounting/power-and-can/index.md): Each driver has two power connectors (JST XH) and two CAN connectors (JST ZH).
- [Thermistor](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/04-mounting/thermistor/index.md): A 100 kΩ NTC thermistor on the motor lets the driver stop before the motor overheats.
- [First setup](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/05-setup/index.md): From a mounted and wired driver to a calibrated, tuned motor.
- [Motor GUI](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/05-setup/motor-gui/index.md): Motor GUI reaches the hardware through the browser's serial port access (Web Serial), which Chromium-based browsers have: Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera.
- [The serial terminal](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/05-setup/terminal/index.md): Motor GUI is the usual way to work with the driver; a plain serial terminal is the alternative, and it is what the console inside Motor GUI is.
- [Motor parameters and calibration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/05-setup/calibration/index.md): Calibration teaches the driver its motor: it checks the magnet and the supply, takes the motor's resistance, inductance and pole pairs from you, computes the current loop gains, spins the motor in open loop to learn the
- [Current limit and loop tuning](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/05-setup/tuning/index.md): Calibration leaves the driver with current loop gains computed for your motor and with conservative velocity and position gains.
- [Saving the configuration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/05-setup/saving/index.md): Nothing you set survives a power cycle until you save it.
- [Operation](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/06-operation/index.md): How a calibrated driver is used: the control modes and what each one does, the two ways to talk to the driver and the two tools on top of them, what happens when something goes wrong, and gripper mode.
- [Control modes](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/06-operation/modes/index.md): The driver is always in one control mode.
- [Over UART](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/06-operation/uart/index.md): The serial port is the interactive way to use the driver: you type a command, the driver answers in text.
- [Over CAN](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/06-operation/can/index.md): CAN is the interface for running a machine: compact frames, a fixed cost per message, up to 14 drivers on one bus, and a host that can be a PC, a microcontroller or a robot control box.
- [With Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/06-operation/python/index.md): The Spectral-BLDC library wraps the CAN protocol: one method per message, and the driver's answers unpacked into attributes.
- [Working in Motor GUI](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/06-operation/motor-gui/index.md): Everyday use of the driver from Motor GUI: moving the motor, watching it, recording what it does, running several motors, and the few things that only work from the console.
- [Errors and recovery](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/06-operation/errors/index.md): When the driver detects a fault it stops the motor, goes to idle, turns the status LED on steadily and sets the error bit in every CAN frame it sends.
- [Gripper mode](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/06-operation/gripper-mode/index.md): A driver can run a gripper instead of a joint: the same board, with a state machine that moves a jaw to a position between open and closed, at a speed, with a current limit that becomes the grip force, and that reports w
- [Firmware](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/07-firmware/index.md): The driver's firmware is open source and released as numbered builds.
- [Releases and versions](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/07-firmware/releases/index.md): A firmware release is a number: 103, 105, 106, … Every release is a tag V<number> in the firmware repository and a GitHub release that carries the image stepfoc-firmware-V<number>.bin, a manifest firmware.json with the i
- [The bootloader](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/07-firmware/the-bootloader/index.md): Every driver shipped with firmware 105 or newer carries a small bootloader in the first 12 KB of its flash.
- [Updating through the bootloader](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/07-firmware/update/index.md): A driver with the bootloader (firmware 105 or newer) is updated over the UART connector or the CAN bus: the host tells the driver to reset, the bootloader waits two seconds for a host, and the host streams the new image
- [Installing the bootloader on an older board](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/07-firmware/bootloader/index.md): A driver running release 103 or older from the main branch has no bootloader: its firmware starts at the beginning of the flash.
- [Building from source](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/07-firmware/building/index.md): The firmware is a PlatformIO project for the Arduino core on the STM32F103CB, in the STEPFOC firmware folder of the firmware repository on the bootloader-version branch.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/08-troubleshooting/index.md): By symptom. The error flags and what clears them are in Errors and recovery; the faults of the firmware that are known and not yet fixed, with what to do until they are, in Known issues.
- [Known issues](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/08-troubleshooting/known-issues/index.md): The faults in the STEPFOC firmware that are known and not yet fixed, and what to do until they are.
- [Firmware release notes](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/appendix/firmware-release-notes/index.md): What changed in each firmware release, from the release notes in the firmware repository, up to the release this site describes.
- [Versions and compatibility](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/appendix/compatibility/index.md): Which firmware release works with which bootloader, Python library, PAR6 runtime and board revision.
- [Hardware revisions](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/appendix/hardware-revisions/index.md): What changed in each revision of the STEPFOC board, and which firmware and which revision of this manual go with it.
- [Theory corner](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/appendix/theory/index.md): The control concepts behind the driver's modes, for readers who want to know why a setting does what it does.
- [Glossary](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/terminology/index.md)
- [Downloads and files](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/cad-files/index.md): Everything to download for STEPFOC, at the versions these pages describe.

## API reference

- [API reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/index.md): Every CAN message and every UART command of the firmware release this site describes, the defaults the firmware starts with, the error flags, and the map from the Python library's calls to the messages they send.
- [CAN frame tool and downloads](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can-tools/index.md): Build or inspect a frame using the command definitions of this manual's firmware release.
- [CAN protocol](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/index.md): CAN 2.0, 1 Mbit/s, 11-bit identifiers.
- [Motion](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/motion/index.md): The commands that move the motor and the frames that come back.
- [Gains and limits](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/gains-and-limits/index.md): The commands that set the loop gains and the limits.
- [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/status/index.md): Data the host asks for with a remote frame (RTR bit set, no data); the driver answers with a data frame with the same command ID.
- [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/system/index.md): Identity, saving, resetting, errors, the watchdog, the heartbeat and the settings.
- [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/gripper/index.md): The commands of gripper mode (#Gripper 1, saved).
- [UART commands](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/index.md): Every command the firmware release this site describes understands over the serial port.
- [Motion](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/motion/index.md)
- [Gains and limits](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gains/index.md)
- [Calibration and motor parameters](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/index.md)
- [Status and utility](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/index.md)
- [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gripper/index.md)
- [Defaults](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/defaults/index.md): The settings of the firmware at the release this site describes: their start values in common.h, and what EEPROM.cpp does with each.
- [Errors and LED states](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/errors/index.md): The flags as the firmware keeps them, the line #Error prints for each, and where each sits in the two bytes of SendRespondStateofErrors (bits numbered from the most significant).
- [Python library](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/python/index.md): The Spectral-BLDC package (Spectral-BLDC-Python, pip install Spectral-BLDC) has one method per CAN message in SpectralBLDC.SpectralCAN, and SpectralBLDC.CanCommunication for the bus.

## Guides

- [Guides](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/guides/index.md): Worked examples with code, from a first Python program to a leg, a gravity-compensated arm and two motors coupled over a network.
- [Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/guides/python/index.md): More examples are in the Spectral-BLDC-Python examples folder.
- [Quadruped leg](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/guides/quadruped/index.md): This guide will cover:
- [Gravity compensation](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/guides/gravity-compensation/index.md): Gravity compensation is a fundamental concept in robotic control that helps counteract the effects of gravity on a robot's joints and links.
- [Bilateral teleoperation](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/guides/bilateral-teleoperation/index.md): The two grippers are virtually coupled to each other, allowing either to act as the master (the haptic interface) or the slave (the manipulator) in the system.

## Support

- [Getting help](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/support/index.md): Before you ask, Troubleshooting goes through the common symptoms, and #Info tells most of what anyone will ask you for.
- [Report a problem](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/support/report-a-problem/index.md): Open an issue in the firmware repository for the driver and its firmware, or in Spectral-BLDC-Python for the Python library.
- [Contributing](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/support/contributing/index.md): This documentation lives in Source-Robotics/STEPFOC-docs.
